## Course outline {.smaller}

1.  Chapter 10: Capital Markets and the Pricing of Risk

2.  Chapter 11: Optimal Portfolio Choice

3.  Chapter 11: Capital Asset Pricing Model

4.  Chapter 13: Investor Behavior and Capital Market Efficiency

5.  Chapter 12: Estimating the Cost of Capital

6.  Chapter 14: Capital Structure in a Perfect Market

7.  Chapter 15: Debt and Taxes

8.  Chapter 17: Payout Policy

9.  Chapters 23-24: Introduction to Long-term Financing

10. Chapters 20 & 30: Options and Risk Management

## Assessment methods {.smaller .dense}

- Overall grade:

  - Continuous assessment

    - Excel group assignment (20%)

    - Pearson Mylab weekly homework (10%)

  - Final exam (70%)\

    - Closed-book, paper-based, on-campus exam.

    - Duration of two hours.

    - Mix of multiple choice questions, calculation questions including
      possibly questions to draw figures with short answers interpreting
      the results, and few short open-answer questions.

    - Formula sheet will be provided and students need to bring a
      calculator.

    - Last year's exam will be provided in November.

- Students need a minimum grade of 8 in the final exam and a minimum
  overall grade of 10 to pass the course.

## Bibliography

- The reference book is Berk, Jonathan and Peter DeMarzo, "Corporate
  Finance," Pearson Education.

- The course will cover the Parts IV, V and VII ... ...but in less
  detail than the book.

- An electronic version of the textbook is available on MyFinanceLab.

## Documents and learning resources {.smaller}

- I will update the slides weekly.

- Blackboard: <https://escp.blackboard.com/> $\Rightarrow$ Additional
  materials and Q&A forum

- Pearson Mylab: MyFinanceLab (access via blackboard)

  - Students are required to complete weekly assignments in
    MyFinanceLab.

  - These homeworks are made available after each lecture block and are
    due before the start of the next lecture block. Late submission will
    not be accepted.

  - Each homework contains five questions that cover a two-hour lecture.
    For four-hour lectures, two such homeworks will be made available
    (covering a total of ten questions).

  - There will be twelve homeworks in total.

  - It is recommended to study the additional exercises for each chapter
    available in the multimedia library.

## Homework grade {.smaller}

- There are twelve homeworks, one for each two-hour lecture block.

- Homeworks are made available after each lecture and they are due one
  week later (before the next lecture starts).

- Each homework is automatically graded on a scale from 0 to 100%. A
  missing homework will receive a grade of zero.

- The homework grade is the average grade in the first eleven homeworks
  multiplied by 20 (to obtain a grade in the 0-20 range).

- The homework grade is worth 10% of the overall grade.
